extracted.intended_audience: authors of life-sciences manuscripts submitting to Nature Portfolio / life-sciences researchers preparing methods and reporting statements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory checklist items for reporting experimental design, statistics, data and code availability, validation of reagents, and ethical/participant information for life-sciences manuscripts submitted to Nature Portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size (n)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exact sample size (n) for each experimental group/condition, given as a discrete number and unit of measurement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that the exact sample size for each experimental group or condition is reported in the figure legend, table legend, main text, or Methods section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct vs repeated measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement on whether measurements were taken from distinct samples or whether the same sample was measured repeatedly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate clearly if measurements are independent biological replicates or repeated measures on the same sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical tests used and sidedness
rubrics_metrics.description: The statistical test(s) used AND whether they are one- or two-sided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only common tests may be described solely by name; describe more complex techniques in the Methods section. State sidedness explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covariates tested
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of all covariates tested
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report which covariates were considered in analyses and how they were modeled or controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of any assumptions or corrections, such as tests of normality and adjustment for multiple comparisons
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the tests used to check assumptions (e.g. normality) and any corrections applied (e.g. multiple comparison adjustments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full statistical parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: A full description of the statistical parameters including central tendency (e.g. means) or other basic estimates (e.g. regression coefficient) AND variation (e.g. standard deviation) or associated estimates of uncertainty (e.g. confidence intervals)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both central estimates and measures of variability or uncertainty alongside reported results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Null-hypothesis testing reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For null hypothesis testing, the test statistic (e.g. F, t, r) with confidence intervals, effect sizes, degrees of freedom and P value noted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give P values as exact values whenever suitable; include test statistics, degrees of freedom and effect sizes together with CIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bayesian analysis reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For Bayesian analysis, information on the choice of priors and Markov chain Monte Carlo settings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report prior distributions, MCMC settings and diagnostics used for Bayesian analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical and complex designs
rubrics_metrics.description: For hierarchical and complex designs, identification of the appropriate level for tests and full reporting of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the level (e.g. animal, organ, cell) at which statistical tests were applied and report outcomes at each relevant level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect size estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of effect sizes (e.g. Cohen's d, Pearson's r), indicating how they were calculated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide effect size measures and describe their calculation so readers can assess practical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software and code availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy information about availability of computer code: For manuscripts utilizing custom algorithms or software that are central to the research but not yet described in published literature, software must be made available to editors and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are strongly encouraged to deposit code in a community repository (e.g. GitHub) and to make central custom software available to editors/reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts must include a data availability statement with accession codes, unique identifiers, or web links for publicly available datasets and a description of any restrictions on data availability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical or third-party data, ensure the statement adheres to Nature's policy; provide accession IDs (e.g. GEO/SRA) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on sex and gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the terms sex (biological attribute) and gender (shaped by social and cultural circumstances) carefully; indicate if findings apply to only one sex or gender and whether sex and gender were considered in study design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide how sex/gender were determined (self-report or assigned), include disaggregated sex/gender data in source data when collected, state if consent obtained, and report sex- and gender-based analyses where performed or justify their absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on race, ethnicity, or other socially relevant groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the socially constructed or socially relevant categorization variable(s) used in your manuscript and explain why they were used
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear definitions of terms used, how categories were provided and methods of classification (self-report, census, administrative data), and avoid using these variables as proxies for other constructs; describe how confounding variables were controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the covariate-relevant population characteristics of the human research participants (e.g. age, genotypic information, past and current diagnosis and treatment categories)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report relevant population covariates; if none to add, refer to prior sections if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how participants were recruited and outline any potential self-selection bias or other biases that may be present
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain recruitment procedures and likely impact of selection biases on results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the organization(s) that approved the study protocol
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full information on protocol approval must also be provided in the manuscript (IRB/IACUC identifiers, approval dates, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justification / power calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement on whether an a priori power calculation was performed and rationale for chosen sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no power calculation was run, provide a rationale (e.g. practical/ethical constraints such as cost or complexity) and justify sample sizes based on precedent or feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of any data or samples excluded from analysis and reasons for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report excluded samples (e.g. transplants excluded due to later-discovered technical issues), justify exclusions and document any consultation with editors if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on replication of experiments and consistency of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how many independent replicates were performed, across what time period or sites, and whether outcomes were consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of randomization procedures and assignment into groups where applicable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how subjects/samples were chosen and assigned, and any constraints or selection criteria used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether experiments and analyses were blinded and justification when not blinded
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report if investigators, assessors, or analysts were blinded to group identity; if not blinded, provide rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials & experimental systems relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must indicate whether each material, experimental system or method listed is relevant to the study
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each listed item (antibodies, cell lines, animals, clinical data, etc.), indicate relevance (yes/no) and provide supporting details when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibodies — listing and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed antibody/reagent table (Antibody/Reagent, Clone, Vendor, Catalogue Number) and validation information demonstrating specificity and cross-reactivity (or lack thereof)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include vendor/catalogue details, describe validation experiments (flow cytometry, IHC, Western blot), controls used (negative controls, knockout controls), and statements about cross-reactivity to other species where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagent and software reporting (versions and tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report software and code used for data collection and analysis with versions (e.g. GraphPad Prism v8.2.0; FlowJo v10.6.1; R v4.1.2; STARsolo v2.7.9a, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a comprehensive list of instruments, plate readers, scanners, and analysis software with versions to enable reproducibility; include links to code repositories when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of key reagents and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation statements describing how critical reagents/methods were validated (e.g. antibodies validated not to cross-react with porcine proteins; functional validations)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize validation evidence (e.g. flow cytometry, IHC, Western blot, depletion experiments) and reference supplementary uncropped images or experimental replicates where applicable.
